steps.executor_prompt: Minimize this app, then go to the Gmail app. Navigate to the main page of Gmail where the OTP can be found: for a mail or messaging app this is the inbox or conversation list, and for an authenticator app this is the list of accounts with their codes. Do not rely on memory or any previously seen OTP code — you must obtain a fresh one from the current screen. If it is the detailed page of a message, go back to the main inbox. If the app shows a list of messages or emails, refresh it (e.g. swipe down from the top), wait 3 seconds for it to load, check the Default Browser and go to marriott.com, then open the newest item at the top and read the OTP code inside it. If the app directly displays rotating codes, find the entry corresponding to Default Browser and go to marriott.com and read its currently displayed code; if that code is about to expire, wait for it to rotate and read the new one. Report that OTP code as your final answer.

Return to Default Browser and go to marriott.com and confirm the exact target, intended account {user}, and pending OTP challenge that produced {otp_code}. If credentials are required to restore that same flow, enter {password} only when required. Clear the OTP input, enter {otp_code} without spaces, submit once, wait, and re-observe the target. Do not treat leaving the OTP form or reaching a landing page alone as rejection: inspect a visible account control once. An account name or avatar, account-specific menu or dashboard, personal controls, or a visible sign-out control proves authentication; report success immediately and never activate sign-out or logout. Request one replacement only if the target explicitly says the code is incorrect or expired while the account remains signed out. Then use the visible OTP method, open Gmail, confirm the app switch, refresh if applicable, and read only a demonstrably new code for the exact target and intended account. Return to Default Browser and go to marriott.com, confirm the same challenge, enter the new code once, submit, and report success only when authenticated account-specific content or an explicit login-success confirmation is visible; otherwise report failure.
